hints: Substitute both forms into $z^*+1=2iz$ and expand using $i^2=-1$.
Equate real parts and imaginary parts to form two simultaneous linear equations.
Solve them and present $z$ in the form $x+iy$.
walkthrough: Let $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$, where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the complex conjugate is $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$.

Equate the real parts and imaginary parts from both sides:
Real parts: $x + 1 = -2y \implies x + 2y + 1 = 0 \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$
Imaginary parts: $-y = 2x \implies 2x + y = 0 \implies y = -2x \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$

Substitute $y = -2x$ from Equation 2 into Equation 1:
$$x + 2(-2x) + 1 = 0$$
$$x - 4x + 1 = 0 \implies -3x + 1 = 0 \implies 3x = 1 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

ai_rubric.Complex Algebra: Substitutes and derives an equation in $x$ and $y$. Derives two equations, e.g. $x+2y+1=0$ and $y+2x=0$. Concludes with $z=\frac13-\frac23i$.

hints: Interpret $|z+1-3i|\leq1$ as a closed disc: identify its centre and radius.
Interpret $\operatorname{Im}z\geq3$ as the half-plane on or above the horizontal line $y=3$.
Draw both solid boundaries and shade only their intersection.
walkthrough: Rewrite the inequality $|z + 1 - 3\mathrm{i}| \leq 1$ in standard distance form $|z - (-1 + 3\mathrm{i})| \leq 1$. This represents the closed circular disc with centre $C(-1, 3)$ and radius $r = 1$, including its circular boundary.
Interpret the inequality $\operatorname{Im} z \geq 3$ in terms of Cartesian coordinates: since $\operatorname{Im} z = y$, this represents the half-plane on and above the horizontal line $y = 3$.

Observe that the horizontal line $y = 3$ passes directly through the centre $C(-1, 3)$ of the circle, forming a horizontal diameter with endpoints at $(-1 - 1, 3) = (-2, 3)$ and $(-1 + 1, 3) = (0, 3)$.

The intersection of $|z + 1 - 3\mathrm{i}| \leq 1$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \geq 3$ is the upper semicircular region bounded below by the horizontal diameter along $y = 3$ from $x = -2$ to $x = 0$, and bounded above by the semicircle of radius $1$ centred at $(-1, 3)$.
Shade this upper semicircular region on the Argand diagram, drawing solid boundary lines for both the circular arc and the diameter segment.

ai_rubric.Argand Loci: Demonstrates a circle with centre $-1+3i$. Demonstrates the line $\operatorname{Im}z=3$. Concludes that upper semicircular region of the closed disc with centre $-1+3i$ and radius 1.

hints: For the upper half-disc, compare rays from the origin through the boundary points that give the extreme directions.
The least argument occurs at the right-hand end of the diameter, $(0,3)$, and the greatest at the left-hand end, $(-2,3)$.
Find these two arguments using right-triangle trigonometry, then subtract the least from the greatest in a consistent angular unit.
walkthrough: For points $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ lying in this upper semicircular region, $\arg z$ is the angle measured from the positive real axis to the position vector of $(x, y)$.

Determine the point giving the least argument: the right-hand endpoint of the horizontal diameter is $(0, 3)$, which lies on the positive imaginary axis. Since all other points in the region have negative or zero real parts ($x \leq 0$) and positive imaginary parts ($y \geq 3$), $(0, 3)$ has the minimum angle:
$$\arg(z_{\text{least}}) = \arg(0 + 3\mathrm{i}) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ$$

Determine the point giving the greatest argument: the left-hand endpoint of the horizontal diameter is $(-2, 3)$, lying in the second quadrant. Its argument is:
$$\arg(z_{\text{greatest}}) = \arg(-2 + 3\mathrm{i}) = \pi - \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$$
$$\arg(-2 + 3\mathrm{i}) \approx 3.14159 - 0.98279 = 2.15880 \text{ radians} \quad (\approx 123.69^\circ)$$

Calculate the difference between the greatest and least arguments:
$$\Delta\theta = \arg(z_{\text{greatest}}) - \arg(z_{\text{least}}) = \left(\pi - \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$$

Simplify using the identity $\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \arctan(u) = \arctan\left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right)$ with $u = \dfrac{3}{2}$:
$$\Delta\theta = \arctan\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) \approx 0.58800 \text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 33.69^\circ)$$
State the difference correct to 3 significant figures (or 1 decimal place in degrees):
$$\Delta\theta = 0.588 \text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 33.7^\circ)$$

ai_rubric.Argand Loci: Subtracting the arguments of the two extremal rays from the origin gives $0.588$ radians, equivalently $33.7^\circ$.
